title: Separation reasons and health disclosures print as the employer name in the delivered DOCX and PDF (25/30 of an authored corpus)
mech: parseOrganizationField only separates a trailing narrative when it sits behind one of three delimiters AND possibleDisclosure flags it, so any employer-box value whose disclosure phrasing the claim-classifier misses — or that has no delimiter, or narrative before the name — is returned whole as the structural identity and printed verbatim as the employer, with no review prompt or receipt note anywhere because the parsed narrative is consumed by nothing.

title: A whole job disappears from the résumé when its title and employer are both blanked and the date field is empty
mech: `organizationIdentity` returns an empty identity whenever a structural field's whole value trips the disclosure classifier with no comma/dash/paren boundary to split on, so both the title and the employer the user typed become "" at the point of read, and `buildExperience`'s OR-filter — which cannot tell a blanked field from a never-filled one — deletes the entire employment row.

title: Real job titles containing a leave phrase are erased whole by the disclosure gate wired into the organization category
mech: parseOrganizationField's whole-value fallback (employment-structure.ts:85) returns identity "" whenever possibleDisclosure() matches the entire field, and evidence-read.ts:399-401 keeps only that identity — so any structural job title or employer name whose own words contain a leave phrase is silently deleted from every generated and exported surface, with the discarded narrative half consumed by nobody.

title: The export sanitizer still runs the claim-admissibility classifier over structural fields and destroys "No Boundaries Training Ltd" on the way into the DOCX and PDF
file: src/lib/evidence-admissibility.ts:568-569 (sanitizeResumeForProfessionalUse -> sanitizeProfessionalLine on role.title and role.company)
mech: sanitizeResumeForProfessionalUse still passes role.title and role.company through sanitizeProfessionalLine, so the claim-admissibility classifier (GAP_PATTERNS[0]) blanks structural employer names at the export boundary — the C2 exemption was applied to sanitizeCareerDossier only, not to the document-building path.

title: A blanked employer is replaced by the fabricated placeholder "Current Company" / "Previous Company" and printed as a real employer
mech: buildExperience substitutes a manufactured employer name ("Current Company"/"Previous Company") whenever the employer field reads empty, and that scaffold is then persisted into the saved résumé version, where C3's harvestHistoricalRoles mistakes the product's own placeholder for a preserved record of the user's employer and "recovers" it into the dossier.

title: An employer name written wholly in a non-Latin script is deleted and replaced with the fabricated placeholder
mech: `isWeakFreeText`'s junk-input test `/^[^\w]+$/` uses a non-Unicode `\w` (`[A-Za-z0-9_]`), so any string containing no Latin letter or digit — i.e. every employer name written wholly in a non-Latin script — is classified as junk, blanked by `normalizeCompany`, and replaced downstream by the hard-coded fallback employer string.

title: Migration writes a DIFFERENT job's employer into a damaged role and labels it "recovered" — reaches the DOCX
mech: historyFor() matches on title OR employer, so a sibling role's saved entries land in the damaged role's match set, and decide() collapses each version to one voice with `values.map(v=>v.trim()).find(Boolean)` BEFORE testing for destruction — the destroyed job's blank is skipped, `someDestroyed` stays false, and the sibling's employer is applied as a unanimous "recovered" answer.

title: A user's own self-description line is parsed as a résumé heading and becomes their employer
mech: harvestHistoricalRoles (src/lib/employment-structure.ts:174-184) admits any line whose split on "|" yields two non-empty segments, guarded only by /^[-•]/ on the first, so product-rendered contact lines, user summaries, "*" bullets and education lines all become {title, company} employment records — and a single such entry is enough for decide() to report "recovered" and write segment two into DossierRole.employer.

title: An unrecognised date range in a heading is restored as the company name
mech: The DATE_RANGE guard only recognises dash-separated numeric-year ranges, so any other user-typed date phrasing in the second segment of a product-rendered "Title | <dates>" heading is harvested as a company and confidently restored as the employer — and because the pre-fix build's own renderer emits that heading from the blanked snapshot, decide() sees the blank snapshot and the rendered line as one version with a single surviving witness and claims unanimity.

title: An empty job title is filled from the sibling role at the same employer and marked "recovered"
mech: historyFor matches history entries on employer alone, so two distinct jobs at one employer land in the same version bucket, where decide()'s per-version find(Boolean) — written to merge duplicate representations of ONE job — collapses two genuinely different real titles to whichever sits first in the array and reports the arbitrary pick as a confident recovery, while the date ranges that would disambiguate are never consulted.

title: The frozen head still runs education through the claims classifier: institution blanked, whole row deleted, persisted
mech: Cluster C's structural-fact protection (roleHasStructure / return-as-typed) was scoped to dossier.roles only, so dossier.education still runs credential/institution/field through the résumé-claims classifier sanitizeProfessionalLine and deletes the row unless credential or institution survives it — on a read path whose output is written back to localStorage.

title: The employer that Cluster C exists to protect is still blanked in every delivered document — and destroyed on disk in the saved snapshot
file: src/lib/evidence-admissibility.ts:568-578 (sanitizeResumeForProfessionalUse), reached from src/lib/pack-export.ts:52,313,336 and src/lib/evidence-admissibility.ts:740 (sanitizeVersion)
mech: sanitizeResumeForProfessionalUse still routes the structural fields role.title/role.company through sanitizeProfessionalLine — the claim-admissibility classifier that Cluster C removed from sanitizeCareerDossier — so any employer name matching a gap pattern is replaced with "" on the export path and, because that same sanitizer runs on every state read and its output is written back to storage, in the persisted resumeVersion snapshot as well.

title: A saved résumé version loses a whole employment row and re-parents its bullet to the employer above — cross-role reassignment, written to disk
mech: sanitizeVersion's legacy branch runs each line of a saved resume through the claim-admissibility classifier, which mis-reads a structural employment heading as an evidence gap and deletes the row while leaving its bullets in place, and the sanitized result is written back to localStorage.

title: A role the pre-fix build deleted outright is never recovered and never flagged, though the saved version still records the job
mech: C3 recovery is a map over surviving role containers, so a role the pre-fix classifier deleted outright has nothing to map over — the whole-container damage class is neither recovered nor flagged, and the migration's own scar-tissue corpus records a roleSurvived flag that is true in all four cases and asserted nowhere.

title: A role whose title and employer are both empty is deleted on reload, even though its dates and bullets survive — and this fires before C3 recovery can run
mech: reviveDossier applies its own stricter role-survival rule (`text(item.id) && (text(item.title) || text(item.employer))`) instead of the canonical `roleHasStructure`, and because it runs inside parseState/loadState it deletes the row before sanitizeCommandCenterState's C3 recovery ever sees it.

title: Recovery confidently assigns the WRONG employer and the WRONG job title when one saved version records two roles that share a title or an employer
mech: decide() collapses every matched historical entry inside one saved version to the first non-empty value ("any surviving witness within a version speaks for it"), so two entries in that version that genuinely disagree on the field never register as a conflict and array order silently becomes the confidently-applied answer, while historyFor matches only on title/employer and never consults the role's dates that would disambiguate them.

title: Rejecting a role's evidence, or excluding its only disclosure, silently deletes the whole employment container from the generated résumé — with nothing in the receipt
mech: buildLaneResume's role loop has two exits for "nothing printable under this heading", and only the later one (empty bullets, lines 302-305) records the omission — the earlier `if (!support.length) return [];` at line 279 drops the whole employment container before any bookkeeping runs, so evidence-level suppression deletes a job from the résumé with no receipt entry.

title: A real job title is erased from the résumé because it contains "maternity leave" — the disclosure classifier is still judging a structural field
mech: The whole-value branch of parseOrganizationField (employment-structure.ts:85) re-applies the claim-admissibility classifier possibleDisclosure to a structural field, so any job title containing the bigram "<maternity|paternity|parental|bereavement|sick> leave" is reduced to identity:"" at every read through getUsableIntake, and the emptied title is then rendered and persisted into the saved résumé version.
